name: Helix Nebula
tagline: The Eye of God — a Sun-like star's death shroud, and our own star's preview.
history: Planetary nebulae have nothing to do with planets — the name survives from William Herschel, who thought their round shapes resembled Uranus. The Helix is the nearest example: a Sun-like star that exhausted its fuel, swelled to a red giant and puffed off its outer layers some ten thousand years ago, leaving a white dwarf whose ultraviolet light makes the shed gas fluoresce in concentric rings. Radial 'cometary knots' stream outward like tadpoles. It is a rehearsal for our own star's future: in about five billion years the Sun will go through the same gentle unbinding.
